## 🗑️ BinSlot – Crafting Table With Automatic Trash Slot

**BinSlot** is a Minecraft mod that adds a custom crafting table featuring a special "bin slot". This slot automatically handles leftover items produced during crafting, helping reduce inventory clutter.

### 🔍 How It Works

When crafting recipes that generate extra items (like empty buckets or bottles), BinSlot will attempt to return them to your inventory. If there's no available space, those items will be discarded automatically using the bin slot.

This behavior mimics the crafting logic of vanilla Minecraft, but improves usability for players who craft large amounts of items or play with recipe-heavy modpacks.

### 🧰 Features

- A custom crafting table with a standard 3x3 grid
- An extra output slot for handling recipe results
- Automatic cleanup of leftover items (e.g. buckets, bottles)
- Supports all vanilla Minecraft recipes
- Helps avoid manual inventory management during crafting

### 🛠 Requirements

- Minecraft Java 1.21.3
- Forge 53.1

### 📌 Notes

- The mod uses Minecraft's standard recipe system.
- It does not require any other mods to function.
- BinSlot is a lightweight quality-of-life addition, especially useful in survival and modded environments.

### 🔧 Future Plans

Planned features may include:
- Customization options for trash behavior
- Compatibility with other mods
- Integration with recipe automation tools

---

If you find a bug or have suggestions, feel free to share them in the project’s issue tracker or discussion page.

title: KindlyTpa
description: Plugin that controls tpa, avoiding users from being tpakilled.
body:
# KindlyTPA

## Overview
KindlyTPA is a lightweight and simple plugin to control tpa in your server instead of installing other big plugins.

## Features.

### Protection System
- Players receive temporary invulnerability after teleportation (configurable duration)
- Prevents ambushes, traps, and _tpakilling _ after teleporting

### User-Friendly Experience
- Simple commands: `/tpa`, `/tpaccept`, `/tpadeny`, and `/tpacancel`
- Clear feedback messages for all actions
- Cooldown system to prevent spam

### Fully Customizable
- All messages are configurable in the config.yml

## Usage
1. Use `/tpa <player>` to send a teleport request
2. The recipient can accept with `/tpaccept` or deny with `/tpadeny`
3. The sender can cancel their request with `/tpacancel`

## Configuration
The plugin features a comprehensive configuration file where you can adjust:
- Protection duration after teleportation
- Request cooldown time
- All message texts with full color code support

```
# KindlyTPA Configuration

# Time in seconds that players will be invulnerable after teleportation
protection-duration: 5

# Cooldown in seconds between TPA requests
tpa-cooldown: 30

# Messages (supports color codes with '&')
messages:
  prefix: "&7[&bKindlyTPA&7] "
  
  # TPA request messages
  request:
    sent: "&aYou have sent a teleport request to &e%player%&a."
    received: "&e%player% &ahas requested to teleport to you. Type &e/tpaccept &aor &e/tpadeny&a."
    no-pending: "&cYou don't have any pending teleport requests."
    expired: "&cYour teleport request to &e%player% &chas expired."
    cooldown: "&cYou need to wait &e%time% &cseconds before sending another request."
    self: "&cYou cannot send a teleport request to yourself."
    not-found: "&cPlayer not found or is offline."
  
  # TPA accept messages
  accept:
    sender: "&aYour teleport request has been accepted. Teleporting in 3 seconds..."
    receiver: "&aYou have accepted the teleport request."
    no-request: "&cYou don't have any pending teleport request from this player."
  
  # TPA deny messages
  deny:
    sender: "&cYour teleport request has been denied."
    receiver: "&aYou have denied the teleport request."
    no-request: "&cYou don't have any pending teleport request from this player."
  
  # Protection message
  protection:
    enabled: "&aYou are now protected for &e%seconds% &aseconds after teleportation."
    disabled: "&cYour teleportation protection has ended."

  # Help message
  help:
    - "&b----- &eKindlyTPA Help &b-----"
    - "&e/tpa <player> &7- Send a teleport request to a player"
    - "&e/tpaccept [player] &7- Accept a teleport request"
    - "&e/tpadeny [player] &7- Deny a teleport request"
    - "&e/tpacancel &7- Cancel your sent teleport request"
```



## Permissions (by default are true)
- `kindlytpa.tpa` - Allows sending teleport requests
- `kindlytpa.tpaccept` - Allows accepting teleport requests
- `kindlytpa.tpadeny` - Allows denying teleport requests
- `kindlytpa.tpacancel` - Allows canceling sent teleport requests

title: Item Guess
description: Do not reveal your item, but try to guess the others!
body:
# ❔ ItemGuess

## 🌃 Abstract

- Plugin is about guessing other players' items to earn the score (or just for fun)
- Native & tested **Minecraft version**: `1.21`

## 💭 Commands

- `/itemguess start` - game start _[**operators** only]_
- `/itemguess stop` - game stop & reset _[**operators** only]_
- `/itemguess set <item>` - set own item for others to guess
- `/itemguess guess <opponent> <item>` - guess someone's item
- `/itemguess help` - list all the possible commands usage

## 🗝 Config


<details>
<summary>Options to config</summary>

- `Feedback Enabled` : extra-feedback messages on guessing item [default: `true`]
- `Scoreboard Enabled` : display or hide scoreboard [default: `true`]
- `Score` : the number of points that players will be rewarded with guessing prizes (only available with _scoreboard_; **integers** only) [default: `1`]

</details>

title: Simple Player Badges
description: A simple Mod that allows you to create, assign and display Badges next to player names in Chat.
body:
![Logo](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/b10f3570663f401ed345908fadb0fda69ea4efe2_0.webp)

**Simple Player Badges** is a mod that enhances your in-game chat by allowing custom player badges to appear next to player names. This mod lets you assign various badges to players and adds a timestamp feature for better chat readability.
The timestamp functionality was inspired by [Beautified Chat by Serilum](https://modrinth.com/mod/beautified-chat-server). Thanks to Serilum for the inspiration, as some of their features were recreated into this mod.


## Configuration:
To configure the badges, you'll need to create a ```badgenames.json``` file in the ```config``` folder of your Minecraft Server. The JSON configuration contains two primary sections:

players: This is where you assign badges to specific players by name.

badges: Here you define the properties of each badge, including its symbol, color, and hover text.

Here's an example configuration:

```
{
    "players": [
        {
            "name": "Player1", 
            "badges": ["badge1", "badge2", "badge3"]
        },
        {
            "name": "Player2", 
            "badges": ["badge2"]
        }
    ],
    "badges": {
        "badge1": { 
            "symbol": "★",
            "color": "gold",
            "hover": "Badge1 Title" 
        },
        "badge2": { 
            "symbol": "α",
            "color": "blue",
            "hover": "Badge2 Title" 
        },
        "badge3": { 
            "symbol": "⚔",
            "color": "red",
            "hover": "Badge3 Title" 
        }
    }
}

```
The configuration file should be saved in UTF-8 format to ensure special characters display correctly.

Operators can use ```/badges reload``` on runtime to update any changes made to ```badgenames.json```.

## Explanation of Fields:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

### players:
- **name:** The Minecraft username of the player.
- **badges:** A list of badge names assigned to the player. Each badge name refers to a badge defined in the badges section.

### badges:
- **symbol:** The symbol or text that will be displayed as the badge next to the player's name in chat. This can include text and symbols.
- **color:** The color of the badge symbol. Use standard Minecraft color names (like gold, blue, red, etc.).
- **hover:** The text that appears when you hover over the badge in chat.

</details>






## To-Do:
- Automatic Config Generation if Config doesn't already exist
- Creating and assigning badges with commands
- Option to enable and disable certain features

title: ApeNet
description: A tiny upgrade to Minecraft Transfer Protocol.
body:
**ApeNet**
A tiny but necessary upgrade to Minecraft Transfer Protocol!

**What is ApeNet?**
ApeNet is a plugin which makes the Minecraft Transfer Protocol Introduced in 1.20.5, more accessible. It adds QoL functions like Server-list, **an EXPERIMENTAL security protocol** and more features to come. It's a really simple, yet useful plugin which can inspure a lot of new projects! 

**Setup Steps**
Easy as 1..2..oh.. It's done
1. Download and put ApeNet in your plugins folder.
2. Set accept-transfers: false --> true on your backend server. Configure and done!

**Config Example**

```
# Command to use for server transfer (default: apenet)
command: apenet

# Enable secure transfer system (default: false)
# VERY EXPERIMENTAL. USE AT YOUR OWN RISK.
# Generates a token.yml. Use the same generated token for every servers to enable a Secure Transfer in-between them.
# It's not full-proof and PROBABLY can be BYPASSED.
secure_transfer: false

# Is this a frontend server? (Only applicable if secure_transfer is true)
frontend_server: false

# Server configurations
servers:
  lobby:
    host: lobby.example.com
    port: 25565
  survival:
    host: survival.example.com
    port: 25566
  creative:
    host: creative.example.com
    port: 25567
```

description: Allows you to change player join/leave or Chat text!
body:
### Player Enhancments
Allows you to change the join/leave or player chat message (also allows yo to run a list of commands when a player leaves or joins)

### How to use:
if you havent changed the config.yml (Root/plugins/Playerenhancments/confg.yml)
the leave/join text shows up as: Player Joined/Left the game/there a now {playercount}/{maxplayers} in the game!
in join/leave text or command you can use these for customization:
- {user} the username of the player
- {playercount} The number of players in the game
- {maxplayers}

in player message text:
- {user} the username of the player
- {message} the text message sent

### Config constumization:

```
joinText: '§e{user} joined the game, There are now {playercount}/{maxplayers} players in the server!' < the tet when a player joins
messageText: '<{user}> {message}' < the text when a player sends a message
leaveText: '§e{user} left the game, There are now {playercount}/{maxplayers} players in the server!' < the text when a player leaves
joinCommands: < the commands when a player joins (it must have ' at the start and end. Example: 'say WELCOME')
- ''
leaveCommands: < the commands when a player leaves (it must have ' at the start and end. Example: 'say WELCOME')
- ''

```

### Default Config.yml:
```
joinText: '§e{user} joined the game, There are now {playercount}/{maxplayers} players in the server!'
messageText: '<{user}> {message}'
leaveText: '§e{user} left the game, There are now {playercount}/{maxplayers} players in the server!'

title: Origins: Palliant
description:
For some, an ill omen. 
For others, the last hope.
body:
Description copied from its entry in the Origins Discord server, seen [here](https://discord.com/channels/734127708488859831/1266280210421121045).

***Created for the Magic Market Jam***

*Rage, rage against the dying of the light...*

**Impact: 2**

**Soul Shepherd:** 
- When non-undead creatures that you haven't harmed die near you, they leave behind Echoes of themselves.
 - Echoes are immune to most damage and vanish after 30 seconds without intervention.
- Right-clicking an Echo with an empty hand will cause it to vanish and grant a Soul Shard.
 - You can consume Soul Shards by right-clicking with one in hand.

> **Spirit Essence:**
> Using a Soul Shard on an Echo will extend its remaining life.


**Fury of The Damned:**
- After consuming a Soul Shard, your next few attacks deal additional Magic damage.
 - This damage is increased against Undead enemies.

> **Mercy in Death:** 
> Killing a creature with a deadly status effect will grant a Soul Shard


**Delay the Inevitable:**
- Consuming a Soul Shard will grant temporary health and briefly protect you from lethal damage.
 - You can share Soul Shards with others by sneaking before using them.

> **Life Transference:**
> Sneaking while using a shard of Prismarine, Quartz, or Glass (any vanilla pane) allows you to sacrifice a quarter of your health to create a Soul Shard.


**Hollow Resonance:**
- Whenever an Echo vanishes near you, you gain Grief. While grieving, you experience 15% fatigue.
 - Fatigue reduces movement speed, break speed, and attack speed.
- If the vanished Echo is one of your tamed creatures, you gain additional effects based on how it vanished.
 - Effects are listed in the Origin menu as tooltips.

> **Overwhelmed:**
> Filling your Grief meter causes you to take damage.


**Soulnumbed:** 
- You gain 15% passive damage resistance.
- You receive 30% less healing.
- You regenerate significantly slower but no longer need full hunger to regenerate.



To add, simply navigate to your world's "datapack" folder and slap this bad boy in there.

title: Jarvis AntiVPN
description: Real-time anti-VPN, proxy and alt blocker for Velocity & BungeeCord — blocks VPNs, proxies, datacenters, Tor and bots across your whole network without banning your real players.
body:
![Demo video of what it looks like in servers and panel](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/abe77659ea369b30ef39def0740a8355aeed67cf.gif)

# Jarvis AntiVPN

### The anti-VPN that **WON'T** block your real players.

A **lightweight Velocity & BungeeCord proxy plugin** backed by a real-time cloud detection network. It blocks VPNs, anonymous proxies, datacenter IPs, Tor and known evasion-network nodes across your whole network — without punishing your legitimate players on mobile data, CGNAT or their home connection.

> **Free in early access.** Detection runs in the JarvisGuard backend; the plugin is a thin, fault-tolerant client. Works on any Velocity or BungeeCord proxy — just paste your license key.

---

## 🎁 Early access — free and fully unlocked

**Sign up and protect your server for free, with everything turned on.** No card, no commitment.

When you register at [jarvisguard.com](https://jarvisguard.com) you get **everything unlocked** at no cost:

- ✅ The full detection engine with **unlimited checks**
- ✅ Real-time, network-wide blocks — one block protects every connected proxy instantly
- ✅ Bot-wave defense and evasion-pattern detection
- ✅ Account Shield, Discord webhooks, multi-tenant panel, country rules

Be one of the first servers on the network while it's free.

[**➡️ Start free now**](https://jarvisguard.com)

---

## Why Jarvis?

The #1 pain of any anti-VPN isn't letting a cheater slip through — it's **wrongly banning a legitimate player**. Someone on mobile data, behind CGNAT or behind their home router is NOT an attacker, yet most cheap plugins kick them anyway.

Jarvis is built the other way around: **when in doubt, the player GETS IN.**

- 🛡️ **One block protects your whole network — instantly.** When Jarvis blocks an IP, that signed verdict propagates to **all** your connected proxies in real time over SSE. No restart, no waiting for a list to refresh.
- 🎯 **Minimal false positives by design.** CGNAT-, mobile- and home-network-aware, so your real community sails in.
- 🕵️ **Detects what cheap plugins don't.** It looks at the connection's behaviour and known evasion patterns, not just a stale datacenter IP list.
- ⚡ **Lightweight & fault-tolerant.** All the heavy logic lives in the backend; the plugin caches locally, applies a signed verdict, and keeps your server running even if the backend has an incident.
- 🌍 **Multi-language panel.** Fully translated (Spanish, English, German, French, Polish, Russian, Turkish), with LATAM-focused support.

---

## What others DON'T see

Most cheap anti-VPNs just query a datacenter IP list. Jarvis weighs the connection's **behaviour**, not just an IP, so it catches what a plain lookup misses:

- 🛰️ **VPNs, anonymous proxies and datacenter IPs** — from live threat feeds kept current, not a stale cached list.
- 🧅 **Tor and known evasion-network nodes.**
- 🔁 **Ban evaders** — surfaced for your staff.
- 👥 **Bot waves** — dampened before they hit your lobby.
- 🏠 **Legitimate home and mobile connections** — recognised so they are NOT penalised (fewer false positives).

---

## 🌐 Real-time network protection

When Jarvis blocks an IP on **any** server of your network, that block propagates **in real time** to **ALL** connected proxies. An attacker who hits one server is blocked everywhere else before they reach your door — one verdict, applied instantly across your whole network. You're not relying on a static list; you're protected by live intelligence.

---

## 🛡️ Account Shield

Built-in **account-theft protection** — a layer almost no anti-VPN offers. It flags signs that an account may be compromised and lists them in the panel for your staff, who can act in **one click**. It protects your players and staff, not just blocks VPNs.

---

## ⚡ Real time (SSE)

Global blocks and panel actions (whitelist, kick, broadcast messages) reach your proxies **instantly** over SSE and invalidate the local cache. What you decide in the panel applies right away — no restarts.

---

## 📊 Honest comparison

| Feature | **Jarvis** | Typical anti-VPN |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| CGNAT / mobile-aware (low false positives) | ✅ Minimal by design | ⚠️ Often kicks them |
| VPN / proxy / datacenter / Tor | ✅ Blocked | ✅ Usually |
| Evasion-network nodes | ✅ Blocked | ⚠️ Often missed |
| Real-time network-wide propagation | ✅ Instant everywhere | ⚠️ Static / periodic list |
| Behavioural analysis | ✅ Multi-signal | ⚠️ Mostly "is it a VPN?" |
| Bot-wave defense | ✅ | ⚠️ Depends on the plugin |
| Account Shield (anti-theft) | ✅ Included | ⚠️ Rarely |
| Signed & verified verdicts | ✅ | ⚠️ Depends |
| Multi-tenant panel + audit | ✅ | ⚠️ Limited |
| Bedrock / Floodgate | ✅ | ⚠️ Depends |

*Category comparison, not against any specific product. Every plugin has its strengths; these are ours.*

---

## 🚀 How to start (4 steps)

1. **Register free** at [jarvisguard.com](https://jarvisguard.com) and copy your **license key** (everything unlocked, no card).
2. **Drop the JAR** into your proxy's `plugins/` folder (Velocity or BungeeCord) and start it once to generate the config.
3. **Paste your key** in `plugins/jarvis/config.yml`:
   ```yaml
   key: "YOUR-LICENSE-KEY"
   ```
   (or set it live with `/antivpn key <key>`). The backend URL and shared secret are fetched automatically.
4. **Done.** Your network is protected instantly. Manage everything from the panel.

### Commands & permissions

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/antivpn key <key>` | Set the license key without restarting |
| `/antivpn stats` | Backend connection status and local cache stats |
| `/antivpn reload` | Reload config, clear cache and resync blocks |

Permissions: `jarvis.command` (use the command), `jarvis.admin` (subcommands + detection notifications), `jarvis.bypass` (never checked — for trusted staff).

---

## 🔒 Privacy & data (network disclosure)

> **This plugin communicates with an external service.** By design, it sends the incoming connection data (such as the IP and UUID) to the JarvisGuard backend, which returns a signed verdict. This is **required** for the anti-VPN to work. It needs an internet connection and a free license key from [jarvisguard.com](https://jarvisguard.com). It is **not an anticheat** — it does not analyse gameplay or game mechanics. If the backend has an incident, your server keeps running normally and protection resumes automatically; the behaviour during incidents is configurable.

The plugin is **closed-source** (All Rights Reserved) and **not obfuscated**, to make platform scanning easy.

Full details: [Privacy Policy](https://jarvisguard.com/legal/privacy) · [Terms](https://jarvisguard.com/legal/terms).

---

## ❓ FAQ

**Will it block my legitimate players?**
That's not the goal — the opposite. When in doubt, the player gets in. Legitimate connections (including mobile and home networks) sail through. Minimizing false positives is the core principle.

**Does it work on Spigot/Bukkit?**
It runs on your **proxy** — **Velocity and BungeeCord**. One filter on the proxy protects your whole network. It's not a per-backend Bukkit/Spigot plugin.

**What if your backend goes down — does my server go down?**
No. The plugin is fault-tolerant: your server stays open, already-known blocks stay blocked via the local cache, and protection resumes automatically. You choose the behaviour during incidents.

**Bedrock / Floodgate?**
Fully supported — Jarvis is tuned to protect your Bedrock and console players without false positives.

**Does it cost anything?**
Not in early access: everything unlocked for free, no card. Paid plans will come later; your server stays protected through the transition.

---

## 📥 Get started

[**➡️ Register free — everything unlocked in early access**](https://jarvisguard.com)
💬 **Discord:** https://discord.gg/5RUbGymKTy
🌐 **Web:** https://jarvisguard.com

*Jarvis AntiVPN — real-time protection that blocks VPNs, proxies and evasion without banning your real players.*

title: Advanced Apples
description: When diamonds and netherite aren't just for armor anymore.
body:
# Advanced Apples

*When diamonds and netherite aren't just for armor anymore.*

---

## What is this mod?

Advanced Apples adds a tier of powerful, late-game food items that scale with the rarest materials in Minecraft. Forget munching on bread and baked potatoes after defeating the Ender Dragon — you deserve better. Much better.

From the humble Diamond Nugget to the terrifyingly powerful Enchanted Netherite Apple, this mod introduces a food progression system that rewards players who have put in the work to reach the end game.

---

## Items

### 🥕 Diamond Carrot
*A carrot infused with the power of diamonds. Crunchy.*

- **Hunger:** 8 🍗🍗🍗🍗
- **Saturation:** 20
- **Effects:**
  - Night Vision (1:30)
  - Absorption I (0:30)

**Crafted** like a Golden Carrot — carrot in the middle, 8 Diamond Nuggets surrounding it.

---

### 🍎 Copper Apple
*Sometimes you just need to breathe underwater and mine faster. Copper delivers.*

- **Hunger:** 4 🍗🍗
- **Saturation:** 8
- **Effects:**
  - Haste I (1:00)
  - Water Breathing (2:00)

**Crafted** like a Golden Apple — apple in the middle, 8 Copper Ingots surrounding it.

---

### 🍎 Emerald Apple
*For when you need the villagers on your side. They'll give you a discount, no questions asked.*

- **Hunger:** 6 🍗🍗🍗
- **Saturation:** 12
- **Effects:**
  - Hero of the Village II (1:30)
  - Luck I (1:30)

**Crafted** like a Golden Apple — apple in the middle, 8 Emeralds surrounding it.

---

### 🍎 Diamond Apple
*An apple so valuable, you'll feel guilty eating it. Do it anyway.*

- **Hunger:** 6 🍗🍗🍗
- **Saturation:** 12
- **Effects:**
  - Absorption II (2:00)
  - Regeneration II (0:10)
  - Resistance I (1:00)
  - Speed I (2:00)

**Crafted** like a Golden Apple — apple in the middle, 8 Diamonds surrounding it.

---

### 🍎 Netherite Apple
*Forged in the fires of the Nether. Fire resistant, just like its ingredients.*

- **Hunger:** 8 🍗🍗🍗🍗
- **Saturation:** 16
- **Effects:**
  - Absorption III (2:00)
  - Regeneration III (0:10)
  - Resistance I (2:00)
  - Fire Resistance (3:00)
  - Strength I (2:00)
- **Fire resistant** — won't burn in lava!

**Crafted** at a Smithing Table — Netherite Upgrade Template + Diamond Apple + Netherite Ingot.

---

### ✨ Enchanted Diamond Apple
*Ancient cities hide many secrets. This is one of the better ones.*

- **Hunger:** 8 🍗🍗🍗🍗
- **Saturation:** 16
- **Effects:**
  - Absorption V (2:00)
  - Regeneration III (0:20)
  - Resistance II (5:00)
  - Fire Resistance (5:00)
  - Speed II (2:00)

**Not craftable.** Found in **Ancient City** and **End City** chests at a 5% chance. The Warden doesn't give it up easily.

---

### ✨ Enchanted Netherite Apple
*You found one. Congratulations. You probably won't find another one for a long time.*

- **Hunger:** 10 🍗🍗🍗🍗🍗
- **Saturation:** 20
- **Effects:**
  - Absorption V (3:00)
  - Regeneration IV (0:30)
  - Resistance III (5:00)
  - Fire Resistance (8:00)
  - Strength II (3:00)
- **Fire resistant** — won't burn in lava!

**Not craftable.** Found exclusively in **Bastion Remnant Treasure Room** chests at a 3% chance. Good luck.

---

## Crafting Materials

### 💎 Diamond Nugget
*Like a gold nugget, but fancier.*

A new crafting material introduced by this mod. Craft 9 Diamond Nuggets from a single Diamond, or combine 9 Diamond Nuggets back into a Diamond. Found in the **Ingredients** creative tab.

---

## FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions)

**Q: Will you backport this mod to older versions?**
A: Follow the project, then ask for it in the comments, and maybe it'll happen if my inner voice feels like it.

**Q: Can you port this to another modloader?**
A: Same thing, different question. Next.

**Q: Which mods are Advanced Apples compatible with?**
A: I have a life, so I didn't test it. If you do test it with other mods and see a conflict, please report it through comments.

**Q: What can I do with this mod?**
A: Whatever you want to. Modpack? Yes. Redistribute? Yes. Make a port of my own? Give credits. Copy the textures to another project? I won't be happy, but the license allows it.

**Q: Where do I report a bug?**
A: Do I look like I have a GitHub page? That's why the comments exist.

---

*Made with unmatched perspicacity, sheer indefatigability, just enough (fixed) crash reports and the utmost dislike of Windows Firewall.*

# SignPlus

> **[SignPlus](https://modrinth.com/mod/signplus) saves the contents of signs when they are destroyed. Place the fallen sign back on the ground, and the text and design will return with it.**

SignPlus preserves the contents of signs when they are broken. Place the dropped sign again, and its text, formatting, colors, glow, back side, and waxed state will return with it.

Have you found a bug? Let me know about it on my [Discord](https://discord.gg/jYrPSz6AGU)!

## Features

### Break it. Keep it. Place it again.

* Preserves all four lines on the **front and back**.
* Keeps text formatting, colors, and glowing text.
* Preserves the waxed state, so protected signs remain protected after placement.
* Supports normal, wall, hanging, and wall hanging signs.
* Supports every vanilla wood type.
* Works when signs are broken by players, explosions, lost support blocks, and other common causes.
* Does not create duplicate or additional sign drops.

### A sign that actually looks like a sign

Held signs are displayed as small versions of their real block models instead of flat inventory icons.

* Preserved text is visible in first and third person.
* Normal and hanging signs use their correct models and wood textures.
* Works in the main hand, off-hand, with two signs at once, and in left-handed mode.
* Smoothly flip a held sign between its front and back sides.
* Other players using SignPlus can see which side you are showing.
* Includes an optional flip sound.

> Press `R`, admire the back side, press it again. Advanced sign technology.

## Settings

With **[Mod Menu](https://modrinth.com/mod/modmenu)** and **[Cloth Config](https://modrinth.com/mod/cloth-config)**, [SignPlus](https://modrinth.com/mod/signplus) settings can be changed directly in the game. # SignPlus

SignPlus сохраняет содержимое табличек при разрушении. Поставьте выпавшую табличку снова — и вместе с ней вернутся текст и его оформление.

* Сохраняется состояние воска, поэтому защищённая табличка после установки остаётся защищённой.

### Табличка в руке теперь выглядит как табличка

Табличка в руке отображается как уменьшенная модель настоящего блока, а не как плоская картинка из инвентаря.

title: The Echo Horror
description: A progressive psychological horror mod that introduces strange anomalies, distant watchers, unexplained encounters, and escalating disturbances as the days pass.
body:
# The Echo Horror

The Echo Horror is a psychological horror mod for Minecraft that slowly transforms a normal survival world into something unfamiliar.

At first, everything seems normal.

Then you begin hearing sounds that shouldn't exist.

You notice signs appearing where you never placed them.

You catch glimpses of figures watching from a distance.

Caves no longer feel safe.

Sleep no longer guarantees rest.

The longer you survive, the more your world changes.

## What Does The Echo Horror Add?

Version 1 introduces the beginning of the horror experience through a progression system that escalates over time.

Features currently include:

* Multiple horror stages that increase as the world progresses.
* Environmental anomalies that become more common over time.
* Predictor events that create tension before larger encounters occur.
* Strange signs containing unsettling messages.
* The Watcher, a mysterious figure that may appear and vanish before you understand what you saw.
* Cave-related anomalies that make underground exploration increasingly dangerous.
* Sleep disturbances that can interrupt the safety of the night.
* The Miner, an unsettling encounter hidden beneath the surface.

## Why Download The Echo Horror?

Unlike many horror mods that rely on constant attacks and jump scares, The Echo Horror focuses on psychological horror.

It is designed to make players question what they saw, whether it actually happened, and whether their world is truly the same world they started in.

The horror escalates gradually over many in-game days, rewarding long-term survival play and building tension naturally over time.

If you enjoy:

* Slow-burn horror,
* Unexplained events,
* Creeping paranoia,
* Subtle environmental storytelling,
* The feeling that Minecraft itself has become wrong,

then The Echo Horror is designed for you.

## Important Information

* This mod is intended primarily for Survival Mode.
* Creating a new world is strongly recommended for the intended experience.
* Many events require multiple in-game days to occur. Short testing sessions may not showcase the full progression system.
* The mod contains psychological horror themes and unsettling content.
* Version 1 represents the beginning of a much larger story and experience planned for future updates.

Your world remembers.

Even when you don't.

How long can you trust what you see?

title: Thunderbolt
description: A simple modpack that doesn't have bloat and is purely optimization mods (except 'OK Zoomer') so you can add your own. Please note that this is tuned for nvidia gpus, specifically ones that are 16xx or newer.
body:
# This modpack is a modpack **without any¹ bloat**.

**Sadly, Thunderbolt does require some setup (read recommended)**

This modpack is made **SPECIFICALLY** for the people who **don't want bloat**/want something to base their own modpack off of

## Why Thunderbolt?

This modpack has compatibility with android, PC, etc.

This modpack **_should_** run better then modpacks like _Fabulously Optimized_

## Recommended

**Recommended** to use these java options (its _ok to skip_ if you dont know what these are):

```
-XX:+UseZGC -Dchunky.maxWorkingCount=1024
```

..also preferrably **_C2ME-OCL_**, but thats just chunk loading speeds.

For the cherry on top, get [**_Nvidium_**](https://github.com/drouarb/nvidium/releases), this is **CRUCIAL** if you want performance, doubles mine, increases my 1% lows, makes my performance more stable, and makes 64 chunk render distance _nothing_

..but it doesnt work on **AMD** gpus, or _NVIDIA_ gpus that are older than the **_16xx_** series

Also, if you play with _very high_ render distances (even at 32, but the issue is more prominent at +32), it is recommended to use **_Longview_**, although that mod _isnt available on all versions_

Additionally, i dont **really** update this modpack unless theres a _decent_ improvement in performance, as its a pain to download it, change it, upload it, add a changelog, etc, just for a small performance upgrade. So _**please**_ take your time to click "Update All" or "Check for updates" if you want max performance.

Benchmarks with a **_RTX 3070_** and a **_Ryzen 5 5500_**

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

```
INFO

Seed: 1234
Same position
Entities turned off
Tick frozen
No nvidium on thunderbolt
Tested with the 1st version of thunderbolt, so expect performance to be better than this.
Same settings, render distance 16
Time: 

TESTS

Thunderbolt: 1117 fps, 1% low 481, 0.1% low 354, average 1070, consistent fps
Adrenaline: 823fps, 1% low 77, 0.1% 41, average 583, VERY inconsistent fps
Fabulously optimized: 731 fps, 1% low 51, 0.1% low 21, average 445, consistent-ish fps
```

</details>

### The cons?
if you want the max fps, you have to manually install some mods due to legal reasons

you might have to update mods yourself if the modpack goes unupdated for awhile


DISCLAIMER: This modpack is tuned to **_Nvidia gpus_**, due to the mod **_Nvidium_**, however it should still work on AMD and <16xx Nvidia gpus.

¹ besides _OK Zoomer_.

title: LastWords
description: Adds funny, editable death messages with 597 defaults, cause-specific message pools, and an in-game GUI editor.
body:
# LastWords

**Funny custom death messages with an in-game editor.**

Because “died” was never funny enough.

---

## Make every death worth reading

LastWords replaces boring vanilla Minecraft death messages with funny, chaotic, dramatic, and fully editable death lines.

Whether someone hugs a cactus, swims in spicy water, gets folded by a skeleton, or gets deleted by a Creeper, LastWords gives every death personality.

---

## Features

- Fully editable custom death messages
- **597 default funny messages included**
- Cause-specific message pools
- Random message selection
- Clean in-game GUI editor
- Add, edit, remove, list, and test messages in-game
- Confirmation menu before deleting messages
- Private death recap for the dead player
- Optional death titles
- Optional death sounds
- Anti-spam protection for rapid deaths
- Built-in placeholders
- No PlaceholderAPI required
- Lightweight and simple to configure

---

## Cause-Based Death Messages

LastWords does not use one generic message for everything.

Messages are split by death cause, so each type of death can have its own random message pool.

Supported examples include:

- Cactus deaths
- Berry bush deaths
- Fall deaths
- Void deaths
- Lava deaths
- Fire deaths
- Drowning deaths
- Suffocation deaths
- Lightning deaths
- Explosion deaths
- Mob deaths
- Boss deaths
- PvP deaths
- Projectile deaths
- Magic and effect deaths
- Fallback and unknown deaths

---

## Discord Webhook Support

LastWords can send death messages directly to Discord using configurable webhooks.

Death messages are posted as clean Discord embeds, complete with the player’s Minecraft head, death cause, world, coordinates, killer, weapon, and a colour that changes depending on how the player died.

Server owners can fully customise the webhook URL, embed title, description, footer, player head display, shown fields, and per-cause colours from the config.

Perfect for community servers that want deaths logged in Discord in a clean and polished way.

---

## Example Default Messages

```text
%player% hugged a cactus. The cactus hugged back with violence.
%player% tried swimming in spicy orange soup.
%player% challenged gravity to a duel and gravity brought receipts.
%player% heard 'ssss' and selected denial.
%player% got folded by calcium.
%player% got bass-boosted into the afterlife.
%killer% folded %player% like a lawn chair using %weapon%.
%player% died so strangely even the plugin looked away.

title: Vanilla Storage Interface
description: A sleek, Vanilla-friendly storage terminal! Access all items – even those nested inside Shulker Boxes – via a searchable, sortable, and scrollable UI. Includes portable Ender Chest access, lag-free visual labels, and many QoL features.
body: ### Note: IRL responsibilities quieted down for the moment so we're back to working on our Minecraft projects, including this one ^^. --- **A sleek, Vanilla-oriented storage terminal mod for Minecraft 1.21.1 (Fabric).** > If you wish to have this mod ported to a newer/older version of the game, or see new block variants or features added, you can create a [Feature Request here](https://github.com/Red-and-White-Fox/Vanilla-Storage-Interface/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) :). If you have any questions, reach out to us in the [Discussions](https://github.com/Red-and-White-Fox/Vanilla-Storage-Interface/discussions) section. > If you find any bugs or issues, please fill out a [🐞BUG report here](https://github.com/Red-and-White-Fox/Vanilla-Storage-Interface/issues/new?template=bug_report.md). --- Tired of digging through massive walls of chests and sifting through countless Shulker Boxes? This mod offers a stupidly simple way to access large quantities of items in one convenient place – using nothing but standard Vanilla inventories. The **Storage Interface** is a smart terminal block. Attach it to a Chest, Barrel, or almost any other block with an inventory to access a unified, **searchable, sortable, and scrollable virtual inventory**. --- ## ✨ Features * **Unified Smart Terminal:** Quickly find what you need with a live search bar, smart sorting (A-Z, Ascending, Descending), and a scrollable grid that bypasses Vanilla slot limits. Enchanted Books dynamically sort by enchantment names, and scroll-extracting smoothly pauses the grid to prevent misclicks. * **Smart Storage Defragmentation:** Press a hotkey to instantly optimize your storage! The server vacuums items, merges partial stacks, sorts them based on your settings, and repacks them to maximize density and free up Shulker Boxes. * **Portable Access:** Access your storage on the go without placing blocks! * **Void Terminal:** Deep-scan all Shulker Boxes inside your Ender Chest. * **Player Terminal:** Browse all Shulker Boxes sitting in your inventory at once. * **Shulker Terminal:** Open a Shulker Box just by hovering over or holding it. * **Zero-Lag Visual Labels:** Place an item in the UI's Ghost Slot to display it on the block like an Item Frame. It renders statically into the chunk mesh – meaning you can have 1,000 of these with **zero frame drops**. Resize, rotate, make it glow! * **Intelligent Auto-Packing:** Utilizes a smart 3-pass algorithm when shift-clicking loose items. The system automatically groups matching items into corresponding Shulker Boxes before packing overflow into empty boxes to save space. * **Stackable Shulker Safety:** Fully compatible with mods that increase Shulker Box stack sizes (like Carpet). It safely auto-splits stacked boxes to prevent duplication or deletion. * **Aesthetic Integration:** Comes in **34 variants** (all 11 wood types + Black Stained Glass). Right-click with a Glow Ink Sac to make the screen glow! --- ## 📖 How to Use 1. **Craft a Frame:** Combine your wood of choice (Planks, Logs, or Stripped) to create a `Storage Frame`. 2. **Craft the Interface:** Upgrade your Frame into the final `Storage Interface`. 3. **Place and Connect:** `Sneak + Right-Click` to place the Interface against any compatible Vanilla storage block. 4. **Interact:** `Right-click` the block to open the terminal. ### ⌨️ Controls & Integrations * **Rapid Movement:** `Shift + Scroll Down` to rapidly pull full stacks. `Ctrl + Scroll Down` for single items. `Shift + Double-Click` to move all matching items. * **Throw Items:** Press your drop key (Default `Q`) to throw items directly out of the terminal. Hold `Ctrl+Q` for full stacks. Hold the key to throw a continuous stream! * **Defragmentation:** Press `Ctrl + S` to compress Shulker Boxes. Press `Ctrl + Shift + S` to fully compress and sort *all* loose items and Shulkers in the terminal. * **IPN Integration:** Operates as a soft dependency for **Inventory Profiles Next**. Dynamically reads live IPN hotkeys and configuration from memory to mimic custom "Move All Items", "Move Matching", and "Include Hotbar" logic natively inside the terminal! * **REI Integration:** Hover over any item in the grid and press `R` or `U` to instantly pull up recipes and uses. **Default Keybinds:** * `V`: Open Void Terminal (Requires Ender Chest in player inventory) * `N`: Open Player Inventory Terminal * `H`: Open hovered Shulker Box * `B`: Open held Shulker Box --- ## ⚙️ Requirements * **Minecraft 1.21.1** (Fabric Loader >= 0.16.14) * **Fabric API** * **Cloth Config API** (Server & Client: Required for settings) * **ModMenu** (Client: Required for client-side settings screen) --- ### Side note: > This mod was primarily developed for our 'Vanilla++' survival server which is still running on 1.21.1 since we were too busy IRL to update our modpack... We are planning on updating the modpack and the server to a newer game version whenever we have the time (summer most likely). As such, we will definitely be updating this mod (and other custom mods made by us) to a newer game version as well. ### Side note 2: > Only limited playtesting has been done so far, so if you encounter any issues, bugs, unintended features or game-breaking behavior, please please do let us know by submitting a [🐞BUG report](https://github.com/Red-and-White-Fox/Vanilla-Storage-Interface/issues/new?template=bug_report.md). Thank you :)

title: CineCam
description: Create smooth camera paths, flythroughs, static shots, and entity-tracking cinematics in Minecraft.
body:
# 🎬 CineCam

**CineCam** is a minimalistic tool for creating cinematic camera animations in Minecraft.

🎥 Create smooth flythroughs, static shots, cuts, camera paths, and entity-tracking scenes — directly inside the game. The mod adds a comfortable Free Cam, a visual point editor, and a quick preview system, so you can build cinematic shots without unnecessary hassle.

## ✨ Features

* 🎮 **Free Cam** for freely moving the camera around the world.
* 📍 **Point-based camera system**: build paths using flight and static points.
* 🌊 **Smooth transitions** between camera points.
* ✂️ **Instant cuts** for sharp cinematic edits.
* 🎯 **Entity tracking** during camera movement.
* 🔧 **FOV, yaw, pitch, hold time, and travel time** customization.
* 👀 **Preview selected** and **Preview all** for quickly testing your scene.
* 💾 **Save and load** scenes from `cinecam/scenes/default.json`.
* 🗺️ **In-world point editing** with visual markers and camera direction lines.
* ⚙️ **Free Cam settings**: speed, sprint multiplier, movement smoothing, FOV, and interface language.
* 🏃 **Motion Capture**: Free camera tracking for creating flythroughs.

## 🚀 Quick Start

1. Enter a world and run:

```mcfunction
/cinecam
```

2. 🎮 Move the Free Cam using **WASD**, **Space**, and **Shift**.
   The sprint key increases movement speed.

3. ⌨️ Press **G** to open the CineCam editor.

4. ➕ Add camera points:

   * ✈️ **+ Flight** — a point for smooth camera movement.
   * 📸 **+ Static** — a point for a static shot.

5. 🔧 Adjust the point settings and press **Apply**.

6. ▶️ Start a preview:

   * 👁️ **Preview selected** — preview from the selected point.
   * 🎬 **Preview all** — preview the full scene.

💡 The **G** key can be changed in the standard Minecraft key bindings menu.

## 📍 Point Settings

Each camera point can be adjusted precisely:

* 📌 **X / Y / Z** — camera position in the world.
* 🔄 **Yaw / Pitch** — camera rotation and tilt.
* 🔍 **FOV** — field of view from `1` to `179` degrees.
* ⏸️ **Hold** — how long the camera stays on this point, in seconds.
* ✈️ **Travel** — how long it takes to move from this point to the next one.
* 🔗 **Next** — the next point number. `0` automatically selects the next point in order.
* 🎯 **Track** — client-side entity ID for tracking. `-1` disables tracking.
* 🌊 **Track smoothing** — smoothness of camera tracking when following a target.

## 🎞️ Transitions and Paths

CineCam supports different camera movement styles:

* 🚁 **MOVE** — smooth movement between points.
* ✂️ **CUT** — an instant cut after the Hold time.
* 🌊 **SMOOTH** — soft acceleration and deceleration.
* ➡️ **LINEAR** — constant movement speed.
* 🌀 **SPLINE** — smooth Catmull-Rom path through nearby points.

🎯 **Pick target** uses the entity you were looking at before opening the editor.

## ⌨️ Commands

```mcfunction
/cinecam
```

🎮 Toggle Free Cam on or off.

```mcfunction
/cinecam on
/cinecam off
```

✅ Explicitly enable or disable Free Cam.

```mcfunction
/cinecam editor
```

📝 Open the CineCam editor.

```mcfunction
/cinecam preview
/cinecam stop
```

▶️ Start or stop the preview.

```mcfunction
/cinecam save
/cinecam load
```

💾 Save or load the scene.

```mcfunction
/cinecam settings
```

⚙️ Open settings for Free Cam speed, sprint multiplier, movement smoothing, FOV, and CineCam language.

## 🌍 In-World Editing

CineCam lets you edit camera points directly in the world:

* 🖱️ Press the attack button while looking at a point marker to select it.
* 🎮 Hold **Alt** and use **WASD**, **Space**, and **Shift** to move the selected point.
* ↔️ **Alt + Arrow Keys** adjust yaw and pitch.
* 🔄 **Alt + Page Up / Page Down** adjust roll.

Visual helpers make scene building easier:

* 🔵 The blue line shows the camera path.
* 🟠 The orange line shows the camera look direction.
* 🌈 The selected point’s XYZ axes are colored red, green, and blue.

## 🎥 Who Is This Mod For?

CineCam is made for trailer creators, cinematic video makers, RP scenes, build showcases, machinima projects, and anyone who needs more control than the default Minecraft camera can provide.

✨ Build scenes, tune camera movement, preview your shots, and film Minecraft like you are using a real cinematic camera tool.

body:
this is the Forge Retail mod! With this mod you can sell items and make tools to get materials faster. The mod adds new ores, new tools and a completly new forging system. To make the new tools you need to melt materials, make casts, cast parts then you can craft the new tools.

To make tools, read these:
1. workstations
2. melting
3. cast making
4. casting
5. last steps

# Workstations:
1. Melting Station
2. Cast maker
3. Casting station

To melt materials you need meltable materials, a bucket and some coal.
Meltable materials:
- Gold
- Iron
- Copper
- Sapphire

Steps:
1. Put any meltable materials, coal and bucket into the melting machine
2. Press the button

To make casts you need a **Cast maker**, **Molten gold** and a stone tool part.
Steps:
1. Craft a Cast maker
2. Craft a stone tool part (any type)
3. Put the stone tool part into the Cast Maker
4. Press the button

# Casting:
To make the final tool parts you need the **Casting station** and the tool materials.

Tool materials:
- Molten iron (for handle only)
- Molten copper (for handle only)
- Molten sapphire (for head only)

Steps:
1. Put the one of the casts and a tool material into the casting station
2. Press the button

# Last steps:
To make the final tool parts you need a tool head and a copper handle (iron handle tools is in the next update).

Steps:
1. Craft together a sapphire tool head and a copper handle
2. Done

# Items:
1. Molds (ingot, pickaxe head, axe head, shovel head)
2. Sapphire juice: a drink item that gives you effects
3. Beanie: cosmetic item

# Selling:
To open the selling gui press **F**.

Steps:
1. Put the product in the first slot
2. Set a price
3. Press the button

This mod is in 1.20.1 forge client and server.

title: DebugBridge
description: Connect MCP clients and local tools to a running Minecraft client for live Groovy scripting, game-state inspection, and a bundled web UI. For mod developers and AI-assisted debugging.
body:
# DebugBridge

A Fabric client mod for Minecraft (1.19, 1.21.11, and 26.2 development snapshots) that exposes game state over a local WebSocket server, plus a Vue web UI for visual inspection. Built for AI-assisted Minecraft development and debugging.

## What It Does

DebugBridge runs a localhost-only WebSocket server (default port 9876, scans 9876–9886) inside Minecraft. External tools — CLI scripts, the bundled Vue web UI, or MCP clients like Claude Code — can inspect and interact with the running game through two complementary APIs:

### Native endpoints (fast, high-level)

Purpose-built Java endpoints that return structured JSON in a single round-trip — no scripting overhead:

| Endpoint | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `snapshot` | Player position, health, food, dimension, gamemode, time, weather |
| `nearbyEntities` | Entities within range: type, position, equipment, distance (with optional `includeIcons` for item textures) |
| `entityDetails` | Full entity info: equipment slots with damage/custom names, vehicle, passengers, attributes, frame contents |
| `lookedAtEntity` | The entity the player is aiming at (raycast) |
| `nearbyBlocks` | Block-entities within range: signs, chests, banners, beacons, furnaces, etc. |
| `blockDetails` | Block-entity contents: sign lines, chest inventory, skull profile, beacon level |
| `screenInspect` | Current open screen/gui: type, title, container slots with item stacks (with optional `includeIcons`) |
| `chatHistory` | Recent client-side chat messages (with optional `includeJson` for styled components) |
| `screenshot` | Capture the framebuffer as JPEG |
| `record_video` | Capture N framebuffer frames (every frame or at a fixed interval) as a JPEG contact-sheet grid or per-frame files |
| `getItemTexture` / `getItemTextureById` / `getEntityItemTexture` | Render item icons as PNG (honors damage, custom model data, dyed leather, player heads) |
| `setEntityGlow` / `setBlockGlow` / `clearBlockGlow` | Highlight entities or blocks with an in-world outline |
| `search` | Search loaded classes by name pattern |
| `status` | Server health and connection info |

Two endpoint families are **gated off by default** in `config/debugbridge.json`: `runCommand` (`run_command_enabled`) sends commands as the player, and the session-control trio `disconnect` / `joinServer` / `quit` (`session_control_enabled`) lets an automation loop leave a world, join a server, or shut the client down. `joinServer` pre-accepts the server resource pack and defers the connect until the client has settled (no loading overlay — joining during the startup resource reload would silently drop the server pack), acking only once the connect attempt has actually started; it's safe to fire the moment the bridge port answers after a launch.

### Groovy execution (`execute` endpoint)

Run Groovy scripts inside the Minecraft JVM with full access to Minecraft APIs via a mapping-aware Java bridge — write Mojang names and they resolve to the runtime (intermediary) names automatically, even on obfuscated builds. Convenience globals `mc`, `player`, and `level` are pre-bound. The sandbox allows file I/O for reading/writing data. Each request has a configurable timeout (default 10s, max 5 min).

```groovy
// Convenience globals already available
println "Player at: " + player.blockPosition().toShortString()
println "Dimension: " + mc.level.dimension().location()

// Load anything else by Mojang name (works on obfuscated builds too).
// Prefer single quotes: double-quoted GStrings interpolate the $ in
// inner-class names like Display$TextDisplay.
def Vec3 = java.type('net.minecraft.world.phys.Vec3')

// Iterate Java collections. Wrap a bulk loop in sync { } so the per-call
// reflective dispatch batches into a single game-thread hop.
sync {
    java.list(level.entitiesForRendering()).each { entity ->
        if (entity.distanceTo(player) < 10) {
            println "Nearby: " + java.typeName(entity)
        }
    }
}
```

## Vue Web UI

The `web-ui/` directory contains a Vue 3 + Pinia + Tailwind app for visual inspection of game state:

- **Dashboard** — Player snapshot overview
- **Entities panel** — Nearby entity list with detail drill-down, equipment icons, glow toggling
- **Blocks panel** — Nearby block-entity browser (signs, chests, etc.)
- **Screen inspector** — Current GUI/inventory slot viewer
- **Groovy inspector** — Drill-down object browser for Java objects
- **Console** — Interactive Groovy REPL connected to the running client
- **Chat history** — Recent client-side messages

**Bundled since v2.0.0** — the mod serves the built UI itself at
`http://localhost:<bridge port + 100>` (default **http://localhost:9976**;
the join-time chat message prints the exact URL as a clickable link).
Loopback-only, static
assets only, and the served page connects to the bridge instance that served
it, so side-by-side game instances each get their own UI. Disable with
`"web_ui_enabled": false` in `config/debugbridge.json`.

For UI development, the dev server still works (with HMR):
```bash
cd web-ui
npm run dev          # → http://localhost:5173
```

The web UI connects directly to the WebSocket server — no MCP layer required.

## Architecture

```
+-----------------------------------+
|  MCP Client (Claude Code, etc.)   |
+---------------+-------------------+
                | MCP Protocol (stdio)
+---------------v-------------------+
|  mcdev-mcp Server (TypeScript)    |
|  Runtime + static analysis tools  |
| github.com/use-ai-for-mc/mcdev-mcp|
+---------------+-------------------+
                | WebSocket (localhost:9876–9886)
+---------------v-------------------+
|  DebugBridge Mod [THIS REPO]      |
|  +-----------------------------+  |
|  | BridgeServer (WebSocket)    |  |
|  | Native endpoints + execute  |  |
|  | Groovy runtime + Java bridge |  |
|  | Mojang mapping resolver     |  |
|  +-----------------------------+  |
+-----------------------------------+
                ^
                | WebSocket (same port)
+---------------+-------------------+
|  Vue Web UI (bundled, :9976;      |
|  npm dev server :5173)            |
+-----------------------------------+
```

## Mojang Mapping Support

The mod automatically downloads official Mojang mappings at startup and uses them to translate human-readable names (`net.minecraft.client.Minecraft`) to the obfuscated names used at runtime. In 1.21.11+, Mojang ships unobfuscated names and mapping is a no-op.

The 26.2 development build targets Mojang-named snapshot classes directly and skips mapping download/remap entirely.

## Security Model

**DebugBridge binds exclusively to localhost (127.0.0.1).** Only processes running on the same machine can connect. The debug port is never exposed to the network.

This is a **development and debugging tool**, not a remote administration system. Anyone with localhost access already has full control over the Minecraft process, so the bridge does not introduce new attack surface.

- **Client-side only** — runs entirely on the client, cannot affect servers or other players
- **No outbound connections** — only startup mapping downloads from Mojang's official APIs
- **Gated features** — `runCommand` and session control are disabled by default (opt-in via config)
- **Developer warning** — first-launch screen informs the user the mod is active; nothing serves until accepted
- **Web UI server** — same loopback-only posture; serves only the static assets bundled in the jar (GET-only, no directory listing, path-traversal rejected)

## Repo Layout

```
mod/
  core/          — Shared Java: BridgeServer, Groovy runtime, mapping resolver, provider interfaces
  fabric-1.19/   — Fabric mod for Minecraft 1.19.x (provider impls + mixins)
  fabric-1.21.11/— Fabric mod for Minecraft 1.21.11 (provider impls + mixins)
  fabric-26.2-dev/— Fabric mod for Minecraft 26.2 development snapshots
web-ui/          — Vue 3 + Pinia + Tailwind inspection app
```

## Installation

Grab the jar for your Minecraft version from the
[GitHub releases](https://github.com/use-ai-for-mc/debugbridge/releases)
(`debugbridge-1.19-*.jar` or `debugbridge-1.21.11-*.jar`), drop it into your
instance's `mods/` folder, and launch with Fabric Loader. Client-side only —
nothing to install on a server. On first run the mod shows a developer
warning in-game and stays inactive until you accept it; the same gate writes
`developer_mode_accepted` into `config/debugbridge.json`. Once accepted, the
bundled web UI is at **http://localhost:9976** (the in-game startup message
prints the exact URL).

## Building

Requires **JDK 21+** for the stable Fabric modules, **JDK 25** for `fabric-26.2-dev` (matches the runtime declared by the snapshot's own version manifest), and **Node ≥20.19** for the web UI.

```bash
# Fabric mods
cd mod
JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home ./gradlew build
# JARs -> mod/fabric-*/build/libs/

# 26.2 development snapshot bridge
cd mod
JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@25/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home ./gradlew :core:test :fabric-26.2-dev:jar

# Web UI
cd web-ui
npm install
npm run dev          # dev server at http://localhost:5173
npm run build        # production build → web-ui/dist/
```

## Testing

Three layers, automated where it pays off:

**1. Core unit tests** — pure JVM, no Minecraft. Runs every PR via `.github/workflows/build.yml`.

```bash
cd mod
JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home ./gradlew :core:test
```

Covers the Groovy bridge runtime, mapping resolver kernel (with stubbed Fabric SPI), and wire-contract tests for every endpoint (using stub providers).

**2. Smoke test against a live mod** — `tools/smoke-test.mjs`. Connects via WebSocket, hits each kernel-candidate endpoint, validates the response. ~30 seconds. Requires Node 22+ for the built-in `WebSocket` global.

```bash
# Smoke test against running 1.21.11 mod
node tools/smoke-test.mjs --port 9876 --version 1.21.11

# 1.19 alongside (default ports: 1.21.11=9876, 1.19=9877)
node tools/smoke-test.mjs --port 9877 --version 1.19
```

**3. Wire-shape regression mode** — same script with `--regression DIR`. Compares each live response's structural shape (key sets at every level, value types) against a captured fixture; fails on drift.

```bash
# Capture baselines once after a known-good build
node tools/smoke-test.mjs --port 9876 --version 1.21.11 \
    --fixtures tools/fixtures/1.21.11

# Later, after deploying a new build, check for drift
node tools/smoke-test.mjs --port 9876 --version 1.21.11 \
    --regression tools/fixtures/1.21.11
```

The shape comparator tolerates value differences (transient game state) but flags any structural change — added/removed keys, type mismatches. **Conditional fields can produce false positives:** `snapshot.target` is only present when the player is aiming at something; `nearbyEntities[].primaryEquipment` only when the closest entity wears something. Capture fixtures from a richly-populated state, or treat conditional-field diffs as expected.

## Usage

### With Claude Code / MCP

Install [mcdev-mcp](https://github.com/use-ai-for-mc/mcdev-mcp) and configure it in your MCP client. The MCP server auto-connects to DebugBridge (scans ports 9876–9886). Tools include:

- **Runtime** (requires this mod): `mc_execute`, `mc_snapshot`, `mc_nearby_entities`, `mc_entity_details`, `mc_looked_at_entity`, `mc_nearby_blocks`, `mc_block_details`, `mc_screen_inspect`, `mc_chat_history`, `mc_screenshot`, `mc_record_video`, `mc_get_item_texture`, `mc_set_entity_glow`, `mc_set_block_glow`, `mc_clear_block_glow`
- **Session control / dev loop** (requires `session_control_enabled`): `mc_join_server`, `mc_leave_server`, `mc_quit_client`, plus `mc_wait_for_bridge` / `mc_wait_until_in_world` for driving rebuild → relaunch → rejoin loops
- **Static** (works offline): `mc_get_class`, `mc_get_method`, `mc_search`, `mc_find_refs`, `mc_find_hierarchy`

### Direct WebSocket

Connect to `ws://127.0.0.1:9876` and send JSON:

```json
{
  "id": "1",
  "type": "execute",
  "payload": {
    "code": "return player.blockPosition().toShortString()"
  }
}
```

Each request gets a matching `{id, type, payload}` response.

## Dependencies Bundled in JAR

- **Apache Groovy 5.0.6** — JVM scripting runtime (Apache-2.0)
- **Java-WebSocket 1.6.0** — WebSocket server (MIT)
- **Gson 2.14.0** — JSON parsing (Apache 2.0)

title: The Beyond - Isleweaver Addon
description: An addon that makes as many End mods as possible play nicely with The Beyond, especially their biomes.
body:
# Isleweaver
Isleweaver is an addon that makes other End mods finally play nice with **The Beyond**, the End overhaul that reshapes the dimension into a deep, layered world of floating islands. That reshaping is exactly what trips other End mods up: built for the old flat void, their structures float, their decorations vanish below the old floor, and their portals land in the wrong place. Isleweaver is the quiet fixer that lets them all share the same End.

## How it works

**Most mods just work — no setup.** Any End mod that registers its biomes the standard way, the shared End biome tags that Fabric and NeoForge mods already follow, is discovered automatically and folded into Beyond's End. No config, no per-mod tinkering. The biomes generate right alongside Beyond's own and keep their distinctive looks and surfaces.

**The big ones get hand-tuned care.** Some larger mods need extra attention to fit Beyond's islands, so they get individual, hand-written fixes:

- **BetterEnd** — its structures, plants, and spires follow Beyond's real terrain instead of hovering over flat void, so they land on solid ground.
- **Enderscape** — its decorations are freed to fill the deep End below y=0, where they used to go missing.
- **Stellarity** — Isleweaver steps aside so its exit portal and altar (the dragon's den) build cleanly, right where they belong.
- **Wover** — kept from overwriting Beyond's terrain, while still lending its biomes their own surface styling.

...and a good handful more, each fix waking up only when that mod is actually installed.

## Good to know

Isleweaver requires **The Beyond** and does its work whenever Beyond owns the End.

BetterEnd and WorldWeaver **WILL** be removed from the main compat list very soon, due to not simply just how unstable it is, but also the fact that they used of AI art, inlcuding suspicions of AI gen code.

title: ParticleProjectileApi
description: A simple api for creating plugins with custom projectiles using particles
body:
Description

This API is designed to allow plugin developers to easily add customized particle projectiles, hence the name. ParticleProjectileApi comes with its own event classes giving the developer a way to cancel an effect when a particle hits, this is quite useful in say mini-games to prevent friendly-fire. It is completely possible to create multiple projectile classes and is encouraged too. When extending the ParticleProjectile class, the developer will be met with five methods: OnHit, OnHitBlock, OnHitEntity, OnPenetrateBlock, OnPenetrateEntity, and OnMove. These methods allow for adding code to run when a projectile hits, passes through something, or moves.

Features

  • method to launch particles (No packets used)
  • Custom events that can be canceled
  • Create multiple projectile classes for different effects
  • More to come!

Usage

MyProjectile.class

package com.aim.coltonjgriswold.projectiles;

import org.bukkit.Location;
import org.bukkit.block.Block;
import org.bukkit.entity.Damageable;
import org.bukkit.entity.Entity;
import org.bukkit.entity.Player;

import com.aim.coltonjgriswold.api.ParticleProjectile;

public class MyProjectile extends ParticleProjectile {

   public MyProjectile() {
     super(Particle.REDSTONE, 0.1, 7.5, 20.0 , 128.0);
     setColor(ParticleColor.fromRGB(255, 0, 0));
     //Initialize a projectile with a color of red, a hitbox with size 0.1 cubed, Mass of 7.5 grams, speed of 20.0 meters/second, max distance of 128 meters
   }

   @Override
   public void OnLaunch(LivingEntity who, Location start) {
     //Do something when launch
   }

   @Override
   public void OnHit(LivingEntity who, Location end) {
     //Do something when reach max distance
   }

   @Override
   public void OnHitBlock(LivingEntity who, Location end, Block what) {
     //Do something when hit block
   }

   @Override
   public void OnHitEntity(LivingEntity who, Location end, Entity what) {
     //Do something when hit entity
   }

   @Override
   public void OnPenetrateBlock(LivingEntity who, Location where, Block what) {
     //Do something when passing through a block
   }

   @Override
   public void OnPenetrateEntity(LivingEntity who, Location where, Entity what) {
     //Do something when passing through an entity
   }

   public void OnMove(Location previous, Location current, double step) {
     //Do something when the the particle moves
   }
}

package com.aim.coltonjgriswold;
import org.bukkit.Material;
import org.bukkit.event.EventHandler;

   }

**Infinite Horizons 1.0.0** is a meticulously crafted, performance-first Minecraft modpack designed for players who want stunning visuals, expansive exploration, and buttery-smooth gameplay at high render distances.

Created by **blissful**.

### Experience the Infinite

This pack transforms vanilla Minecraft into a breathtaking open-world adventure. With **Terralith** + **Tectonic** as the foundation, the Overworld feels truly alive — featuring dramatic mountain ranges, lush river valleys, intricate cave systems, and diverse, hand-crafted biomes that reward exploration. **Let the horizons be infinite.**

title: Bounty Enchantment
description: Server sided enchantment that increases mob XP drops.
body:
![Icon](https://github.com/FireDragon91245/Bounty-Enchantment/raw/1.21.3/src/main/resources/assets/bounty_enchantment/icon.png)
# Bounty Enchantment

**Items:**  
![Sword](https://github.com/FireDragon91245/Bounty-Enchantment/raw/1.21.3/src/main/resources/assets/bounty_enchantment/sword.png)
![Axe](https://github.com/FireDragon91245/Bounty-Enchantment/raw/1.21.3/src/main/resources/assets/bounty_enchantment/axe.png)

A simple server-sided enchantment that increases the amount of dropped XP from mobs.
The multipliers for levels 1–5 are configurable in the `bounty_enchantment.json` inside the server’s config directory.

## Config
```json
{
  "levelMultipliers": [
    1.25,
    1.5,
    1.75,
    2.0,
    2.5
  ],
  "maxXpCap": 32767,
  "allowOffhand": false,
  "debug": false
}
```
`levelMultipliers`: Configure the multipliers for each level, where the index is the level  
`maxXpCap`: A hard cap to limit XP per mob (must not exceed a god particle’s worth (`2^15-1` or `32767`))  
`allowOffhand`: If set to true, allows the use of the offhand item bug. (Offhanded item takes over enchantments from main-hand item (for example, bow takes Looting from sword); in this case, ranged weapons would also take over the Bounty enchantment if an item with Bounty is held in the main hand)  
`debug`: Print calculated XP amounts in the server logs (only for debugging)

title: Create: Galvanized
description: Improve your Iron & Steel equipment with Zinc!
body:
**Improve your Iron & Steel equipment with Zinc! Galvanization adds much more durability and a bit more enchantability to tools and armor.**

 

## Getting Started

First you'll need to get a Galvanized Upgrade Smithing Template, which can be obtained from mineshafts, village blacksmith or pillager outpost chests. Once you have it, it can easily be duplicated with Zinc Ingots and Tuff.

![](https://media.forgecdn.net/attachments/description/null/description_74d15d77-bf54-469e-8060-4a19088137a5.png)

It can also be created from scratch using a sequenced assembly recipe.

![](https://media.forgecdn.net/attachments/description/1541133/description_5775276d-4c8d-4b97-92a7-f08e6bf03d0b.png)

To upgrade your equipment, simply put it in a Smithing Table along with the template and a Zinc Ingot.

![](https://media.forgecdn.net/attachments/description/null/description_e2c19a50-ddda-46d2-bcee-4229d1ad36eb.png)

Galvanized equipment can also be repaired with Zinc Ingots alongside their default repair material (configurable via tag).

![](https://media.forgecdn.net/attachments/description/1541133/description_3fb790e5-3da7-479d-8ec5-948b4a0b2ec6.png)

Galvanization is generally more effective on tools than armor. While galvanized tools have 60% more durability, galvanized armor only has about 33% more, however it does have a slightly higher enchantability bonus.

 

## Requirements:

[Create](https://modrinth.com/mod/create) (required). For galvanized Steel equipment, you will need [Create: Alloyed](https://modrinth.com/mod/create-alloyed) (optional).

title: Box3JS
description: Box3JS is a Minecraft server-side mod inspired by Box3 coding style. You don’t need to write Java — just use TypeScript to build scripts.
body:
# Box3JS — Minecraft Scripting Engine

> **Beta** — APIs may change during early development. Feedback is welcome.

**No Java, just TypeScript.** Build Minecraft minigames, RPG systems, and world mechanics with scripts that hot-reload in seconds.

Built on Mozilla Rhino, Box3JS brings the Box3 coding style to Minecraft servers. Write TypeScript, run it instantly — no JDK, no Gradle, no server restarts.

## Features

- **TypeScript-first** — Full type declarations (`.d.ts`) with bilingual JSDoc, auto-complete in any editor
- **Box3-compatible API** — World, Entity, Player, Voxels, Storage, Database, HTTP, remoteChannel
- **110+ Minecraft extensions** — Scoreboards, BossBars, teams, world border, particles, fireworks, potions, custom blocks/items/sounds registration, and more
- **Client-side scripting** — Custom HUD, keyboard input, audio playback, client-side SQLite & HTTP
- **Project isolation** — Run multiple script projects independently, each with its own scope and callbacks
- **Sandbox mode** — Test safely; roll back all script-made changes on stop
- **Standalone compilation** — `/box3script compile` packages your script into a distributable JAR

## Quick Start

```
/box3script create mygame
```

```
npm install && npm run build
```

```
/box3script sandbox mygame
/box3script start mygame
```

Full guide: [https://docs.box3lab.com/box3js-mc](https://docs.box3lab.com/box3js-mc)

## License

title: Pickup
description: Pick up items by right clicking them!
body:
# Pickup

Pickup is a mod that lets players pick up items by right-clicking them. (or whatever their interact key is set to) It works completely server-side so any vanilla client can join. The only client-side feature is the configuration modification system, an extra system for modifying the mod's configuration while the server is running (as opposed to editing the JSON and restarting).

![Showcase of the mod](https://github.com/thecreeper3326/pickup/blob/26.1.x/showcase.gif?raw=true)

## Configuration
### Core mechanics
* Enable/disable modified pickup behavior - toggles the mod's right-click-to-pick-up feature
* Enable/disable vanilla pickup behavior - toggles Minecraft's walk-over-to-pick-up system

Both of the above can be turned on and off independently of each other.
You can also override the default item entity's hitbox with custom dimensions. This makes targeting easier because the vanilla item entities have a fairly small hitbox. (The hitbox has a maximum limit of 1x1x1 blocks to prevent cramming)

### Extras
* Item name and count overlay - shows the name and amount of the item the player is looking at
* Glowing item overlay - gives the targeted item a glowing effect
* Overlay range - how far the player has to be for the overlays to appear (separate from actually being able to interact with them)
* Use default range - uses the player's `EntityInteractionRange` attribute instead of the provided value
* Pickup to current hand - instead of stacking to the player's hotbar/inventory like normal, a picked up item will be placed in the active slot of the player if it is empty

### Editing configuration
Aside from editing the JSON while the server is offline, you have a couple other options to get the mod configured if you have it installed on your client.
1. Command - Running `pickup_config` as an admin will open a nice GUI where you can edit the config and apply it without restarting the world.
2. ModMenu - With Mod Menu, you can access the same config GUI by opening the Mod list and clicking the configure icon.

Operator permissions are required. All configuration changes are validated server-side to catch any invalid values. Once again, the client mod is completely optional!

## Prerequisites
All you need is a version of Fabric API that is for the same minecraft version, no extra config libs.
